props.classMechanic_text:
ILLUSIONIST MECHANIC — PHANTASMS

“Thought made form. Command made motion.”

What Are Phantasms?

  • Phantasms are entities of pure energy that can take on different sizes and forms—even exact replicas of you.
  • They do not think, talk, or reason. They obey, they don’t improvise.
  • They follow only simple, one-clause commands and cannot infer meaning beyond those words.

Design intent: You shape intent into action. Keep commands crisp (“Move to the door.” “Attack that archer.” “Guard me.”).

Core Traits & Stats

Attributes & Defenses

A Phantasm uses your base Attributes and your Defenses.

MP: none. Status: Immune to all status effects.

Phantasmal Vitality (PV)

PV = your base Insight die size + your level. Track per Phantasm.

All Phantasm attacks (when applicable) target Magical Defense.

Turn Economy — Commanding Phantasms

  • No Initiative: Phantasms do not take their own turns.
  • On your turn, you can spend an action to command one or more Phantasms (as allowed by the spell’s wording).
  • You may create a Phantasm and immediately command it in the same action. After that first command, it takes a full action on a later turn to command again.
  • You cannot command Phantasm A and then also create Phantasm B in the same action.
  • Unless a spell says otherwise, you may have up to 3 Phantasms active. Further casts beyond 3 simply fail.

Shattering & End of Scene: A Phantasm shatters if its PV reaches 0, if you fall to 0 HP, or if you leave the scene. You can also shatter them through your skills, spells, or at will.

Vitality Examples (PV)

Your Insight DieYour LevelPhantasmal Vitality (PV)Notes
d6511PV = 6 + 5
d81018PV = 8 + 10
d101222PV = 10 + 12

Adjust for your table’s die sizes / level cap.

Create & Command — Step by Step

  1. Cast/Conjure: Create 1 Phantasm (or more, if the spell says so). Place it per spell text.
  2. First Command (free with creation): Give a single, simple clause (“Move to the door.” “Attack the ogre.” “Guard me.”).
  3. Later Turns: Spend a full action to command Phantasms again (one or more, as permitted by the spell).
  4. Resolve Actions: Phantasm attacks target Magical Defense. They are immune to statuses.
  5. Track PV: When PV hits 0, the Phantasm shatters.

Command Craft: Use location (“north doorway”), subject (“that archer”), and mode (“block”/“attack”/“follow”). Avoid conditions that require judgment (“until safe,” “if threatened”).

Quick Reference

  • Phantasms use your Attributes/Defenses; no MP; status-immune.
  • PV = Insight die size + Level.
  • No turn on Initiative; you command them on your turn.
  • Create + immediate command in the same action; later commands cost a full action.
  • Max 3 active unless a spell says otherwise.
  • Shatter on PV 0, if you 0 HP, or if you leave the scene.

Play Tips (Table-Ready)

  • Position first. Your opening command should place or screen.
  • Economize commands. Use wording that covers multiple Phantasms (“All Phantasms: form a wall in front of us.”) if the spell allows it.
  • Protect PV. Rotate fresh Phantasms forward; shatter low-PV ones to deny enemy on-hit riders.
  • Synergy: Pair with zones, illusions, or terrain that benefits extra bodies/blocks.

Worked Examples

Example A — Mirror Guard (creation + command): You conjure a Phantasm adjacent to you and immediately command: “Guard me.” It moves to interpose and will block the next enemy trying to pass. Next round, you spend an action to command again: “Hold that doorway.”

Example B — Multi-Unit Order (as wording allows): You already have 3 Phantasms out. You spend 1 action: “All Phantasms, attack the ogre.” Each uses your stats, targets Magical Defense, and resolves per spell. None act outside your command window.

Pocket Card (Hand to Players)

  1. Create a Phantasm (spell). Uses your Attributes/Defenses. PV = Insight die size + Level.
  2. Immediate Command (same action): give a simple one-clause order.
  3. Later Commands: spend an action on your turn to command again (one or more, as the spell allows).
  4. Limits: Max 3 active. Status-immune. Attacks vs Magical Defense.
  5. Shatter: PV 0, you 0 HP, or you leave the scene (or shatter at will).

Bf7Byi1jgUI8An8V.facet_description:
You can now have up to 4 active Phantasms, but one of them must necessarily be Numen. Also, you cannot have more than one Numen Phantasm active at a time. This Phantasm cannot be used in any of the Illusionist’s Skills or Spells.

Numen is bound by the same set of special rules as any other Phantasm, with the following exceptions:

  • Numen Phantasms cost 50 MP to cast.
  • Numen’s Phantasmal Vitality equals twice your base Insight die size plus your level.
  • Once active, Numen has its own turn and a single action. It does not benefit from Spells that grant additional actions. Numen’s turn can be taken either before or after the Illusionist’s turn.

When creating a Numen Phantasm, choose one essence, which dictates Numen’s damage type:

  • Ravana — Physical
  • Asura — Light
  • Diablos — Dark

The target hit by Numen suffers [HR + 14] damage.

Damage dealt by Numen ignores Resistances and Immunities.

The range of the attack is determined by your current weapon.

Skill Enhancement Lv. 20 ― Numen’s on-hit damage increases to 18.

Skill Enhancement Lv. 40 ― Numen’s on-hit damage increases to 20.

props.class_lore: Illusionists are masters of deception and manipulation, blurring the lines of reality to protect their allies and disorient their foes. Thriving on uncertainty, their presence on the battlefield is marked by unpredictability, sowing chaos across the enemy lines. But an Illusionist's powers go beyond mere trickery: they can conjure material Phantasms that mimic their own form, sending these mindless doppelgangers into the fray on their behalf.
